    (certificate : GibbsCertificate State) (candidate : FiniteLaw State) :

    (certificate : GibbsCertificate State) :

maturity_record.invariant: The finite Donsker–Varadhan objective is bounded by the certified log partition, with equality exactly at the supplied full-support Gibbs optimizer.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The result is parameterized by GibbsCertificate, whose strict-support and log-density fields make the finite logarithmic boundary explicit. It does not extend the equality to arbitrary measures, unbounded potentials, or an optimizer whose existence has not been certified.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The uniform zero-potential certificate from the shared foundation supplies a normalized full-support optimizer; unequal candidates have a strictly positive KL gap and therefore cannot attain equality.

declaration_statements.fep060_coordinateELBO_decomposition:
theorem fep060_coordinateELBO_decomposition
    (actualPrior referencePrior : FiniteLaw Latent)
    (actualKernel referenceKernel : FiniteKernel Latent Observation)
    (hprior : ∀ latent, 0 < referencePrior latent)
    (hkernel : ∀ latent observation,
      0 < referenceKernel latent observation) :
    jointELBO actualPrior referencePrior actualKernel referenceKernel =
      -finiteKL actualPrior referencePrior -
        conditionalKL actualPrior actualKernel referenceKernel
declaration_statements.fep060_coordinateKL_nonnegative:
theorem fep060_coordinateKL_nonnegative
    (prior : FiniteLaw Latent)
    (actual reference : FiniteKernel Latent Observation) :
    0 ≤ conditionalKL prior actual reference

maturity_record.invariant: A finite joint ELBO separates exactly into a prior-coordinate score minus an expected conditional KL remainder, and that remainder is nonnegative.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The decomposition assumes every reference-prior and reference-kernel atom is strictly positive so all logarithmic rewrites are sound. Conditional KL nonnegativity is proved for the project's totalized finite divergence, but no zero-reference extended-real interpretation is claimed.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Distinct actual and reference kernels yield a positive conditional remainder; matching kernels collapse only that coordinate penalty while leaving the prior-coordinate score visible.

theorem fep061_meanFieldCoordinate_optimum_iff
    (fixed : FiniteLaw Fixed) (candidate target : FiniteLaw Coordinate)
    (hfixed : ∀ x, 0 < fixed x) (htarget : ∀ y, 0 < target y) :
    meanFieldCoordinateFreeEnergy fixed candidate target = 0 ↔

theorem fep061_meanFieldCoordinate_reduction
    (fixed : FiniteLaw Fixed) (candidate target : FiniteLaw Coordinate)

    meanFieldCoordinateFreeEnergy fixed candidate target =

maturity_record.invariant: Holding one supported mean-field factor fixed reduces the coordinate free energy exactly to finite KL, whose unique zero is the supported target factor.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The fixed and target laws have full support on finite carriers. The theorem is a one-coordinate optimum with the other factor held fixed; it does not prove global convergence of alternating mean-field updates or handle continuous variational families.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: A candidate different from the full-support target has strictly positive coordinate free energy, whereas selecting the target attains the exact zero optimum for any full-support fixed factor.

rows.title: Fixed-Sample Importance-Weighted Jensen Bound

declaration_statements.fep062_iidProduct_importanceJensen:
theorem fep062_iidProduct_importanceJensen
    (base : FiniteLaw Sample) (sampleCount : ℕ) [NeZero sampleCount]
    (weight : Sample → ℝ) (hweight : ∀ sample, 0 < weight sample) :
    ∑ sampleTuple, iidProductLaw base sampleCount sampleTuple *
        Real.log (sampleMeanWeight sampleCount weight sampleTuple) ≤
      Real.log (∑ sampleTuple, iidProductLaw base sampleCount sampleTuple *
        sampleMeanWeight sampleCount weight sampleTuple)
declaration_statements.fep062_fixedSample_importanceJensen:
theorem fep062_fixedSample_importanceJensen
    (sampling : FiniteLaw Sample) (weight : Sample → ℝ)
    (hweight : ∀ sample, 0 < weight sample) :
    ∑ sample, sampling sample * Real.log (weight sample) ≤
      Real.log (∑ sample, sampling sample * weight sample)
declaration_statements.fep062_expectedImportanceWeight_positive:
theorem fep062_expectedImportanceWeight_positive
    [Nonempty Sample]
    (sampling : FiniteLaw Sample) (weight : Sample → ℝ)
    (hsampling : ∀ sample, 0 < sampling sample)
    (hweight : ∀ sample, 0 < weight sample) :
    0 < ∑ sample, sampling sample * weight sample

maturity_record.invariant: For a positive fixed sample count and positive weights, the IID product-law expectation of the log sample-mean weight is at most the log of its expected sample-mean weight.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The carrier is finite, NeZero excludes sample count zero, and every weight is strictly positive before Real.log is used. The positive-expectation witness additionally assumes a nonempty carrier and full-support sampling law.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Nonconstant positive importance weights on a nonempty finite carrier give a genuinely random positive sample mean; a one-sample law recovers the base finite Jensen inequality.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: native Lean compile of fep062_iidProduct_importanceJensen, fep062_fixedSample_importanceJensen, and fep062_expectedImportanceWeight_positive for positive weights.

    finiteKL
        ((FiniteKernel.deterministic (fun _ : Input => ())).predictive actual)
        ((FiniteKernel.deterministic (fun _ : Input => ())).predictive reference) <

maturity_record.invariant: Passing two finite full-support laws through the same strictly positive finite channel cannot increase their finite KL divergence.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Input is nonempty, both input laws have strict support, and every channel atom is strictly positive; these conditions force reference-predictive support and avoid the project's totalized-log boundary. This is stronger support than the most general measure-theoretic data-processing theorem.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Any noisy positive channel acting on unequal full-support input laws exercises a genuine contraction comparison. Separate identity and complete-coarsening witnesses cover deterministic zero-entry channels: identity preserves finite KL and complete coarsening strictly reduces it for unequal laws. These do not weaken the support premises of the primary theorem or identify singular native infinity with the project's totalized finite convention.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: native Lean compile of fep063_finiteChannel_klDataProcessing and fep063_referencePredictive_fullSupport with all three support certificates, plus fep063_identityChannel_preservesKL and fep063_constantChannel_strict.

own_novelty_record.carrier_delta: Adds two full-support input laws, a normalized finite channel, and predictive-law support propagation.

touching_relations.rationale: Finite-channel contraction is paired with the native nonnegativity of the pre-channel KL quantity; no unsupported finite-to-measure identification is introduced.

declaration_statements.fep064_rateDistortion_weakDuality:
theorem fep064_rateDistortion_weakDuality
    (joint : FiniteLaw (Source × Code))
    (distortion : Source → Code → ℝ)

    (hmultiplier : 0 ≤ multiplier)
    (hrate : rateLower ≤ mutualInformation joint)
    (hdistortion :
      distortionLower ≤ expectedDistortion joint distortion) :

      rateDistortionLagrangian joint distortion multiplier

    ∃ optimizer : FiniteLaw (Source × Code),
      RateDistortionFeasible source distortion budget optimizer ∧

maturity_record.invariant: Separately certified lower bounds on finite mutual information and expected distortion combine into a lower bound on their rate–distortion Lagrangian for every nonnegative multiplier. Supporting theorems now additionally establish an attained information minimum for every nonempty finite fixed-source distortion-feasible set, an actual Lagrangian-infimum weak-duality bound, and an attained strictly positive optimum at fair Boolean Hamming budget one quarter.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The theorem assumes both component lower bounds rather than deriving a dual function. The supporting attainment theorem instead derives primal optimizer existence from compactness and the continuous zero-safe entropy expression for mutual information, requiring only a feasible finite joint with fixed source marginal. Infimum-derived weak duality requires nonnegative distortion and multiplier; zero-multiplier dual value requires a nonempty code alphabet. Neither general strong duality, dual attainment, a closed-form interior rate function, nor general optimizer uniqueness is claimed. The structural-proxy disposition and primary theorem remain unchanged: the primary theorem still assumes separately certified component lower bounds, while the independently reviewed supporting theorems establish finite optimizer attainment and infimum-derived weak duality.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Positive multipliers make both certified components contribute, while setting the multiplier to zero reduces the Lagrangian exactly to mutual information and gives dual value zero. A concrete quarter-crossover Boolean joint makes the interior budget feasible, while every independent fair-source joint has distortion one half, forcing the attained quarter-budget optimum positive. Negative budgets are infeasible, zero budget forces a unique diagonal joint, and half budget has two distinct independent information minimizers.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: native Lean compile of fep064_rateDistortion_weakDuality and fep064_zeroMultiplier_boundary, all three supporting attainment/duality/ informative-interior declarations, and the zero-dual, negative-budget, nonunique-half-budget, and unique-zero-budget boundaries. The actual optimizer is derived, never supplied as a certificate field.

own_novelty_record.new_invariant: Certified rate and distortion lower bounds combine by weak Lagrangian duality.
own_novelty_record.carrier_delta: Adds a finite source–code joint law, distortion function, and explicit nonnegative multiplier without optimizer existence.

touching_relations.rationale: Rate--distortion weak duality is accompanied by the measure-native nonnegativity law for the mutual-information ingredient's KL semantics.

findings.exact_correction: If actual and reference rows differ at a latent state of positive actual-prior mass, the conditional remainder is positive. Differences confined to zero-prior rows need not contribute. Matching kernels make this coordinate penalty zero while leaving the prior score visible.

A sampling law assigning positive probability to two different weight values gives a genuinely random sample mean. Nonconstant weights off the sampling support do not. A one-sample law recovers finite weighted Jensen.
